correctness.rationale: The exact \(2n\)-vertex cubic graph and constraints are defined. Counting crossing edges gives \(|D|\ge n\). With rung indicators and counts \(x,y,z\), we have \(|D|=n+z-x\). Local selected-degree at least two and unselected-degree at least one exclude simultaneous empty and singleton rungs when \(z-x\le1\). Singleton/three words force a unique full rung and opposite singleton blocks across the seam (\(2n\) candidates); empty/full words force empty runs of length at most two and full runs of length at least two, producing the four-periodic patterns or a unique length defect (\(n\) shifts for odd \(n\)). Every candidate was directly checked. Exhaustive subsets at \(3\le n\le9\) and independent finite-state transfer at \(3\le n\le60\) agree; the infinite proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: The Möbius twist on a natural cubic circulant makes the standard half-order capacity-domination bound attainable only in one congruence class modulo four. The theorem gives the exact optimum, a necessary-and-sufficient description of every attaining source set, and closed labelled counts: four, twice the rung count, or three times the rung count, according to the congruence class. This exhibits a mathematically sharp structural rigidity and a one-source penalty, considerably more informative than a generic bound or finite table.
